VERDICT: REJECT

The proposed answer $t$ is almost certainly wrong. The Schur square $C \odot C$ is spanned by coordinatewise products of pairs of codewords, and it is generally much larger than $C$. For generalized Reed-Solomon codes of dimension $t$, the Schur square has dimension $\min(n, 2t-1)$, which exceeds $t$ whenever $t \ge 2$. Here $t \ge 2s \ge 2$, so the answer $t$ conflicts with the basic behavior of the square.

The proposed solution also gives no derivation. It cites an unspecified result from "the literature" and says the constraints "ensure" the dimension is preserved, without showing why. The HRS structure (hyperderivatives of order up to $s-1$ at each point) changes the count relative to GRS, so the exact value must come from that structure. I did not verify the exact formula, but $t$ is not it.

CONFIDENCE: 4
